original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Exact lower bounds on masked P112 decoder cost (floor 64) for: every decoder with at most 8 rank-1 terms (any supports, any characteristic-0 field); decoders mixing rectangles and Ferrers atoms with at most 8 pieces; 9-term decoders with rank M = 8; the KFAM T-block cost C(T) = 8 for rank-1 rectangles (all six orbits) and for the interleaved menu (orbit 0 fully, orbits 1, 3, 4 in part). Not covered: 9-term decoders with rank M = 9, any m >= 10, mixed decoders with >= 9 pieces, multi-wire terms.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a decoder with larger-rank children; the work instead proves where masked rank-1 and Ferrers-atom decoders cannot go below 64, which bounds the effective child rank obtainable from the P112 mask. No supplier, coefficients or kappa.
bottleneck_link: Any masked P112 decoder below COPY64 would change the eight centre-copy calls; these results close that route for every decoder with at most 8 terms and for all rank-M-8 nine-term decoders.
stop_rule: Stop each lemma at the first proof or the first explicit cost <= 63 decoder; none was found.
evidence: verify.py reruns the exact enumerations, the SAT/DRAT shards and the LP-dual certificates; saved log and receipt in data/.

open_questions.question: Does every decoder with 9 terms and rank P = rank Q = 9 cost at least 64?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the smallest case of the wall not covered: rank M = 8 is closed, so a 63-cost nine-term decoder, if it exists, has two P-classes and two Q-classes of frames.
open_questions.first_step: Prove the row-rigidity gating lemma: some P- or Q-class of every rank-9 decoder has a row-rigid complement of at least 40 lines (random line sets of that size always are, 28 or fewer never).
open_questions.blocked_by: An INT-M8-Step-A-type no-extra-zero fact for sub-patterns L minus Lambda; only Lambda = one line and one A2 triple were checked (DRAT).

open_questions.question: Does the wall (cost >= 64) hold for every m >= 10?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Cost 63 forces a term of cost at most 6 when m = 10, and cheap terms meet every frame; the monotone rows (frames, lines, global rank) only reach 18.9, so the proof must use coefficients.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the frame-defect analysis (per-frame defect of rank m - 8) to m = 10 via the P- and Q-class lemma.
open_questions.blocked_by: No classification of rank-9 completions; the previously conjectured rank-9 form 'G8 plus one rank-1 correction' is false (explicit counterexample on an A2 triple).

open_questions.question: Do the piece-count and floor results extend to mixed decoders with 9 or more pieces?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Any decoder with a genuine Ferrers atom has at least 9 pieces; the smallest open mixed case is seven rectangles plus one two-level atom.
open_questions.first_step: Repeat the rank-M-8 core analysis with the atom's two pieces as ordinary pieces, using MIX-8 (no genuine atom at 8 pieces).
open_questions.blocked_by: Rectangle results bound piece sums, not atom floors.

open_questions.question: Audit the COVERSAT cut-model encoding, and solve KFAM orbit 2.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Orbits 1, 3, 4 are closed by DRAT only through the cut model (exact Lemma-B rank cuts and the ratio lemma), whose encoder is unaudited; orbit 2 completes the family.
open_questions.first_step: Independent re-derivation of cutenc.py (finite-field witnesses and the ratio lemma) against exact ranks; re-run the five open orbit-2 shards with certified no-goods.
open_questions.blocked_by: Orbit 2 has almost no free cells, so the polynomial systems are large (about 50 equations).
